collocationTask.explanationRu: Escape (или avoid) detection — остаться незамеченным. Finding — находка, opening — открытие магазина, а noticing после escape не употребляют.

nuance.text: Smoke [[detection]] is the job of a small sensor in the ceiling.
nuance.explanationRu: Detection — обнаружение: датчик замечает дым, анализ выявляет болезнь. Investigation — расследование, долгое выяснение обстоятельств.

reverse.text: Police have launched an [[investigation]] into the fire.
reverse.explanationRu: Расследование начинают: launch an investigation into something. Detection — сам факт обнаружения, его не «запускают».

fixIt.text: Thanks to the early [[revelation]] of the tumour, she needed only minor surgery.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Раннее выявление» болезни — early detection. Revelation — откровение или разоблачение, к медицине не подходит.

wordFormation.text: Dogs are trained in the [[detection]] of explosives and drugs.

rewrite.original: Nobody noticed what the thieves were doing for two years.
rewrite.frame: The thieves ____ for two years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Escape или avoid detection — остаться незамеченным.

words.definitionEn: the state of being kept in prison or another official place, often without trial
words.senseNote: Также — наказание в школе: остаться после уроков (get a detention). Здесь — содержание под стражей.
words.situation: Someone is held by the police or the state, for example in a cell, camp or special centre.

examples.text: The suspect will remain in [[detention]] until his case goes to court.
Lawyers were not allowed to visit him during his [[detention]].
Passengers without valid visas were taken to a [[detention]] room at the airport.

texts: The journalist was freed after ten days in [[detention]].
Rights groups criticised the [[detention]] of peaceful protesters.
Conditions in the [[detention]] centre were described as appalling.

badCollocation.noteRu: Задержка зарплаты — late payment of wages или delayed wages. Detention — содержание человека под стражей.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Held in detention (или custody) — содержаться под стражей. Арест — under arrest, capture — «поимка», а hostage употребляют без in: held hostage.

nuance.text: After two years in [[detention]], she was finally released.
nuance.explanationRu: Arrest — сам момент задержания (make an arrest, under arrest). Detention — период, когда человека держат под стражей: two years in detention.

reverse.text: Police made three [[arrests]] after the match.
reverse.explanationRu: Задержать кого-то — make an arrest. Detention — не действие полиции, а сам срок содержания под стражей.

fixIt.text: He spent six months in [[conclusion]] before the case against him was dropped.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Заключение под стражу» — detention (или custody). Conclusion — «вывод» или «окончание», это ложный друг переводчика.

wordFormation.text: Human rights lawyers challenged the [[detention]] of the students.

rewrite.original: The police held him for two days without charging him.
rewrite.frame: He was held in ____ for two days without charge.
rewrite.explanationRu: Held in detention — содержался под стражей.

words.definitionEn: to gradually become worse in quality, condition or strength
words.situation: Someone's health, a relationship or an old building slowly gets worse over time.

examples.text: Her condition [[deteriorated]] overnight, and she was moved to intensive care.
Relations between the two departments have [[deteriorated]] so badly that they barely speak.
Wooden window frames begin to [[deteriorate]] if they are not painted every few years.

texts: Food will [[deteriorate]] quickly if the fridge breaks down.
Doctors warned that his eyesight could [[deteriorate]] further.
We cannot let the situation [[deteriorate]] into open conflict.

badCollocation.noteRu: Deteriorate — «ухудшаться» самому, без дополнения. «Ухудшить ситуацию» — worsen или make the situation worse.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Здоровье ухудшается — health deteriorates. Spoil — о еде или испорченном празднике, damage требует дополнения, descend — «спускаться».

nuance.text: Relations between the neighbours [[deteriorated]] after the argument over the fence.
nuance.explanationRu: «Отношения испортились» — relations deteriorated (или went sour). Spoil — испортить что-то (праздник, сюрприз) или об испортившейся еде.

reverse.text: Don't let one bad review [[spoil]] your whole weekend.
reverse.explanationRu: Испортить кому-то выходные или праздник — spoil. Deteriorate — ухудшаться само по себе, дополнения у него нет.

fixIt.text: His health [[aggravated]] quickly during the long winter.
fixIt.explanationRu: Aggravate — «усугубить» что-то (aggravate an injury), ему нужно дополнение. «Здоровье ухудшилось» — his health deteriorated.

wordFormation.text: Doctors noticed a sharp [[deterioration]] in her breathing overnight.

reply.context: A friend asks about your grandfather: "How is he doing after the operation?"
options: Much better, thanks! He's deteriorating really fast now.
His physiological condition has undergone a deterioration of moderate severity.
He was doing well, but he's deteriorated a bit since the weekend, so we're worried.
reply.explanationRu: Deteriorate — ухудшаться, поэтому «мы волнуемся» звучит логично. Радоваться, что дедушка deteriorating, — противоречие, а второй ответ звучит как медицинская справка.

words.definitionEn: to create a strong relationship, agreement or connection through hard work
words.senseNote: Здесь — «налаживать, выстраивать» (forge ties, forge an alliance); значение «подделывать» (forge a signature) не тренируем.
words.situation: Two people, companies or countries work hard to build a lasting partnership, friendship or agreement.

examples.text: The two rival airlines [[forged]] a partnership that now lets passengers book both companies' flights on one ticket.
The new principal wants to [[forge]] closer links between the college and local employers.
At university she [[forged]] friendships that are still going strong thirty years later.

texts: Small firms often struggle to [[forge]] ties with big retailers.
A difficult shared project can [[forge]] real team spirit.
The treaty helped the two former enemies [[forge]] a lasting peace.

badCollocation.noteRu: С документами forge значит «подделать»: forge a contract — подделать договор. Заключить договор — sign a contract; forge — про союзы и связи.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ an alliance with a rival company
collocationTask.explanationRu: Forge an alliance — заключить союз, выстроить партнёрство. Do, take и draw с alliance не сочетаются: говорят form, build или forge an alliance.

nuance.text: Over ten years, the museum has [[forged]] close ties with schools across the region.
nuance.explanationRu: Forge ties — выстроить прочные связи ценой усилий. Make с ties и partnership звучит неестественно: make обычно в make friends, make contacts.

reverse.text: She found it easy to [[make]] friends at her new school.
reverse.explanationRu: Заводить друзей — make friends. Forge сочетается не с людьми, а с отношениями: forge a friendship, forge ties.

fixIt.text: The new ambassador hopes to [[adjust]] closer ties between our two countries.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Наладить связи» — не adjust (подстроить, отрегулировать), а forge ties: создать прочные отношения.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How did the trade fair in Berlin go?"
options: Really well. We forged some useful links with two German suppliers.
Really well. We forged a lovely lunch at a German restaurant.
Affirmative. Strategic linkages were forged with supply-side stakeholders.
reply.explanationRu: Forge links — наладить полезные связи. Обед словом forge не описывают. Третий ответ звучит как канцелярский отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The two companies built their partnership during the financial crisis.
rewrite.frame: The partnership between the two companies ____ during the financial crisis.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the partnership was forged — союз был выстроен.

words.definitionEn: a method or set of principles that reliably produces a particular result
words.senseNote: Здесь — «рецепт, способ добиться результата» (a formula for success); математическая или химическая формула — базовое значение.
words.situation: Talking about a proven method or combination of things that usually leads to success or a particular result.

examples.text: The show's [[formula]] never changes: three amateur cooks, one mystery ingredient and a strict time limit.
There's no magic [[formula]] for building a successful start-up; it takes luck and years of hard work.
After weeks of talks, the parties agreed on a [[formula]] for sharing power in the new coalition.

texts: Good food and friendly staff: that's the [[formula]] behind their success.
Many romantic comedies follow the same predictable [[formula]].
There is no simple [[formula]] for raising happy children.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Формула успеха» — a formula for success, с предлогом for. The formula of — о химической или математической формуле: the formula of water.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Формула успеха — a formula (или a recipe) for success. Receipt — чек, а не рецепт; form — бланк или форма, formation — образование или строй.

nuance.text: Negotiators finally found a [[formula]] that allowed both sides to claim victory.
nuance.explanationRu: Formula — выработанная схема, способ решить задачу; так говорят и о переговорах. Recipe — прежде всего кулинарный рецепт, а в переносном смысле чаще a recipe for disaster.

reverse.text: Could you send me your [[recipe]] for that lemon cake?
reverse.explanationRu: Кулинарный рецепт — recipe. Formula рядом с тортом прозвучит как химическая формула или детская смесь.

fixIt.text: There's no secret [[receipt]] for a happy marriage; you just keep talking to each other.
fixIt.explanationRu: Receipt — чек из магазина, а не «рецепт». Способ добиться результата — formula: a formula for a happy marriage.

wordFormation.text: Critics called the film [[formulaic]]: the plot followed every rule of the genre.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Your team hit every target this year. How did you do it?"
options: Honestly, the formula was very kind to us and gave us extra time.
The formula underpinning our performance shall be disclosed in due course.
Honestly, there's no magic formula. We just planned carefully and talked a lot.
reply.explanationRu: No magic formula — «нет волшебного рецепта». Formula не может быть «добра» к людям, это не человек. Второй ответ звучит как пресс-релиз, а не разговор с коллегой.

words.definitionEn: to develop a plan, policy or idea carefully, working out all the details
words.situation: A team or government carefully develops a detailed plan, policy or strategy before acting.

examples.text: The ministry has six months to [[formulate]] a new policy on air pollution in cities.
Before collecting any data, researchers should [[formulate]] a clear hypothesis.
Our team spent the whole afternoon [[formulating]] a response to the client's complaint.

texts: Parents and teachers met to [[formulate]] new rules on mobile phones.
It took the scientist years to [[formulate]] her theory of memory.
The new manager must [[formulate]] a clear strategy for growth.

badCollocation.noteRu: Решение не formulate, а make или reach: make a decision. Formulate — разрабатывать план, политику, теорию.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Разработать стратегию — formulate a strategy. Compose — сочинять музыку или письмо, perform — исполнять, pronounce — произносить.

nuance.text: The committee spent months [[formulating]] detailed guidelines for online teaching.
nuance.explanationRu: Formulate — продумать и разработать план, правила, теорию. Form — создать, образовать: form a committee, form a group. Продуманную разработку правил form не передаёт.

reverse.text: The students [[formed]] a committee to organise the graduation party.
reverse.explanationRu: Создать комитет или группу — form. Formulate относится к идеям и планам, а не к организациям.

fixIt.text: Our department has [[composed]] a new policy on working from home.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Составить политику, план» — не compose (сочинять музыку, текст), а formulate или draw up.

wordFormation.text: The [[formulation]] of the new safety rules took almost a year.

rewrite.original: The committee needs to develop a clear plan for the new library.
rewrite.frame: A clear plan for the new library needs to ____ by the committee.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив после needs to: needs to be formulated.

words.definitionEn: forward, onward or out into view; mostly used in fixed formal phrases
words.senseNote: Почти всегда в устойчивых сочетаниях: set forth, put forth, come forth, hold forth, and so forth, back and forth.
words.situation: Formal writing or speech about presenting ideas publicly, or about someone stepping out to be seen or heard.

examples.text: After the appeal on television, three new witnesses came [[forth]].
The treaty sets [[forth]] clear rules for fishing in shared waters.
My uncle loves to hold [[forth]] on politics at family dinners.

texts: The committee put [[forth]] a bold plan to save the old harbour.
Nobody has come [[forth]] to claim the lost wallet.
Spring brings [[forth]] fresh green leaves on every tree.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Продвигаться вперёд» с проектом — move forward или go ahead. Forth живёт в книжных сочетаниях: put forth, set forth, come forth.

collocationTask.prompt: set ___ the terms of the agreement
collocationTask.explanationRu: Set forth (книжн.) — «излагать»: условия, правила, доводы. Set about — «браться за дело», set apart — «выделять», set upon — «нападать».

nuance.text: In her opening speech, the lawyer set [[forth]] the main arguments for the defence.
nuance.explanationRu: Set forth — книжное «изложить»: доводы, условия, правила. С глаголом set слово forward так не работает; в нейтральной речи говорят set out или put forward.

reverse.text: I'm really looking [[forward]] to seeing you next week.
reverse.explanationRu: «Ждать с нетерпением» — только look forward to. Forth — книжное слово из сочетаний put forth, set forth.

fixIt.text: Bring your laptop, charger, notes and so [[further]].
fixIt.explanationRu: «И так далее» — and so on или более книжное and so forth. And so further — калька с русского.

words.definitionEn: willing to give information or talk openly about something
words.senseNote: Здесь — «охотно рассказывающий» (not very forthcoming about...); значение «предстоящий» (the forthcoming elections) проще.
words.situation: Describing whether a person is willing to answer questions and share details openly.

examples.text: The manager wasn't very [[forthcoming]] about why three senior staff had suddenly left.
When we asked about the missing money, the treasurer was surprisingly [[forthcoming]] and showed us every receipt.
Teenagers are rarely [[forthcoming]] about their social lives, so don't take it personally.

texts: The minister was not [[forthcoming]] with details of the deal.
My landlord is never very [[forthcoming]] about repair dates.
Ask her directly; she's usually quite [[forthcoming]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Общительный человек — outgoing или sociable. Forthcoming — «охотно делящийся сведениями», обычно в ответ на вопросы.

collocationTask.prompt: She wasn't very ___ about her reasons for leaving.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Forthcoming about — «охотно рассказывающий о чём-то». Upcoming — «предстоящий», oncoming — «встречный», outgoing — «общительный»; с about их так не используют.

nuance.text: The new tenant is polite but not very [[forthcoming]] about her past.
nuance.explanationRu: Forthcoming — готов делиться сведениями, отвечать на вопросы. Outgoing — общительный по характеру; с about его не сочетают, и о готовности рассказывать оно не говорит.

reverse.text: He's very [[outgoing]] and loves meeting new people.
reverse.explanationRu: Общительный, любящий компании — outgoing. Forthcoming говорит о готовности рассказывать, а не о характере в целом.

fixIt.text: The company has been less than [[upcoming]] about the risks of the new product.
fixIt.explanationRu: Upcoming — «предстоящий». Неохотно делиться сведениями — be less than forthcoming about something.

reply.context: A friend asks: "So, did your landlord explain why the rent is going up?"
options: Not really. He was very forthcoming, so he refused to tell me anything.
Not really. He wasn't very forthcoming; he just muttered something about costs.
Regrettably, the lessor was insufficiently forthcoming regarding the aforementioned increase.
reply.explanationRu: Not very forthcoming — «не особо рвался объяснять». Very forthcoming значит «охотно всё рассказал», это противоречит отказу говорить. Третий ответ — канцелярит, а не разговор с другом.

words.definitionEn: to encourage a feeling, skill or idea to develop over time
words.senseNote: Здесь — «способствовать развитию» (foster creativity); значение «взять ребёнка на воспитание» (foster a child) не тренируем.
words.situation: A school, company or community creates conditions that help good qualities, habits or relationships grow.

examples.text: Good teachers [[foster]] curiosity by letting students ask questions instead of just memorising facts.
Open-plan offices were supposed to [[foster]] teamwork, but many employees simply wear headphones all day.
The street festival aims to [[foster]] understanding between the city's many different communities.

texts: Shared meals can [[foster]] a strong sense of family.
The government offers tax breaks to [[foster]] innovation in small firms.
Coaches try to [[foster]] a positive attitude after every defeat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Продажи и прибыль не foster, а boost или increase. Foster — про качества, отношения и идеи: foster trust, foster creativity.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Развивать качество — foster. Raise и bring up — растить детей, educate — давать образование; с creativity их не сочетают.

nuance.text: Good libraries [[foster]] curiosity and a love of reading.
nuance.explanationRu: Foster — создавать условия, чтобы качество развивалось: foster curiosity. Educate — учить, просвещать людей; с curiosity или love of reading его не сочетают.

reverse.text: The charity [[educates]] the public about healthy eating.
reverse.explanationRu: Просвещать людей о чём-то — educate someone about something. В значении «развивать» foster относится к качествам и отношениям, а не к людям.

fixIt.text: Our aim is to [[raise]] a culture of openness in which everyone feels free to speak.
fixIt.explanationRu: Культуру, атмосферу, доверие не raise, а foster — «создавать условия для развития». Raise — растить детей или поднимать.

reply.context: At a staff meeting, your manager asks: "How can we get different departments to work together more?"
options: We could foster the printer in the corridor so everyone shares it.
We could run joint projects. That would foster cooperation without forcing it.
Dunno, just foster some good vibes or whatever.
reply.explanationRu: Foster cooperation — «способствовать сотрудничеству». Принтер нельзя foster: глагол говорит о развитии качеств и отношений. Третий ответ слишком небрежен для рабочей встречи.

words.definitionEn: weak and uncertain, and therefore easily damaged or destroyed
words.senseNote: Здесь — о мире, экономике, отношениях: «хрупкий, шаткий»; буквальное значение (fragile glass) проще.
words.situation: Describing a peace deal, economy or relationship that could easily break down or collapse.

examples.text: The ceasefire is still [[fragile]], and both sides accuse each other of breaking it.
After two years of recession, the recovery remains [[fragile]] and could easily stall.
Their friendship was still [[fragile]] after the argument, so she chose her words carefully.

texts: The two parties formed a [[fragile]] coalition after the election.
Tourism is a [[fragile]] industry that depends on good news.
Her confidence is still [[fragile]] after months out of work.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Уязвимый к чему-то» — vulnerable to. Fragile не требует предлога: a fragile economy.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перемирие, которое легко сорвать, — a fragile ceasefire. Breakable — о бьющихся предметах, fragmentary — «отрывочный», thin — «тонкий».

nuance.text: Relations between the two neighbours remain [[fragile]] after years of conflict.
nuance.explanationRu: Fragile — о том, что легко разрушить: мир, отношения, восстановление экономики. Flimsy — «хлипкий»: тонкая ткань, шаткая конструкция, неубедительная отговорка.

reverse.text: He gave a [[flimsy]] excuse for missing the meeting.
reverse.explanationRu: Неубедительная отговорка — a flimsy excuse. Fragile описывает то, что может разрушиться, а не слабый довод.

fixIt.text: Experts warn that the peace between the two countries is still very [[breakable]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Breakable говорят о посуде и других предметах. Хрупкий мир, хрупкая экономика — fragile.

wordFormation.text: The crisis exposed the [[fragility]] of the country's banking system.

reply.context: Your colleague asks: "Should we launch the new product now or wait until spring?"
options: I'd wait. Consumer confidence is still pretty fragile after the price rises.
Let's launch now. Our confidence is so fragile that nothing can shake it.
One would posit that the market's fragile disposition necessitates postponement.
reply.explanationRu: Fragile — «шаткий, легко разрушимый». Во втором ответе fragile противоречит словам «ничто не поколеблет». Третий звучит как научная статья, а не рабочий разговор.

words.definitionEn: permission to run a business using a big company's name and products
words.senseNote: Здесь — деловое значение «франшиза»; «право голоса» (формальное) и «серия фильмов» (a film franchise) — другие значения.
words.situation: Someone pays a large company to open a shop or café using its brand name and system.

examples.text: She bought a coffee-shop [[franchise]] instead of starting a business from scratch.
Each [[franchise]] pays the parent company a share of its monthly profits.
The pizza chain now has over 300 [[franchises]] across the country, mostly run by local families.

texts: Opening a [[franchise]] usually costs less than launching your own brand.
The gym [[franchise]] in our town closed after two years.
He signed a ten-year [[franchise]] agreement with a burger chain.

badCollocation.noteRu: Страховая «франшиза» по-английски — excess (брит.) или deductible (амер.). Franchise — право работать под чужим брендом.

collocationTask.prompt: open a ___ of a well-known coffee chain
collocationTask.explanationRu: Работать под брендом сети — open a franchise. Filial значит «сыновний, дочерний», а не «филиал»; department и division — отделы внутри компании.

nuance.text: Instead of opening its own shops, the company sells [[franchises]] to local owners.
nuance.explanationRu: Franchise — право вести бизнес под чужим брендом; точка принадлежит местному владельцу. Branch — филиал, которым владеет сама компания, поэтому продавать branches владельцам нельзя.

reverse.text: The bank is closing its [[branch]] in our village next month.
reverse.explanationRu: Отделение банка, которым владеет сам банк, — branch. Franchise — бизнес, который владелец купил право вести под брендом.

fixIt.text: My uncle bought a [[filial]] of a popular pizza chain and now runs it with his sons.
fixIt.explanationRu: Filial — «сыновний», а не «филиал». Купить право работать под брендом сети — buy a franchise.

wordFormation.text: [[Franchising]] lets a brand grow quickly without opening its own shops.

reply.context: A friend says: "I'd love to open a café, but I've never run a business."
options: Have you considered a franchise? It's when you insure your café against fire.
Might I propose the acquisition of a franchise, thereby mitigating operational risk?
Have you considered a franchise? You'd get a known brand, a tested menu and training.
reply.explanationRu: Franchise — право работать под известным брендом, с его меню и поддержкой. Страховка тут ни при чём. Второй ответ звучит как бизнес-презентация, а не совет другу.

words.definitionEn: used to show that you are giving your honest opinion, even if it is unwelcome
words.senseNote: Здесь — вводное «честно говоря» (Frankly, ...); значение «откровенно» (speak frankly) проще.
words.situation: Before giving an honest opinion or admitting something that the other person may not want to hear.

examples.text: [[Frankly]], your essay is too long, and the main argument gets lost halfway through.
I'm not sure the new app is worth the money; [[frankly]], I preferred the old one.
Thanks for asking my opinion, but [[frankly]], I think the plan is doomed.

texts: Well, [[frankly]], I expected more from such an expensive hotel.
The service was slow and, [[frankly]], a little rude.
She's talented, but [[frankly]], she isn't ready to lead a team.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Честно говоря» — frankly или frankly speaking, но не frankly saying: это калька с русского.

collocationTask.prompt: Quite ___, I don't think he's the right person for the job.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Quite frankly — «если уж честно», перед неприятной правдой. Openly, directly и sincerely вводными словами в начале фразы не бывают.

nuance.text: [[Frankly]], I think we're paying far too much for this office.
nuance.explanationRu: Frankly в начале фразы — «честно говоря», перед неприятной правдой. Sincerely — «искренне» (sincerely hope, sincerely thank); вводным словом его не ставят.

reverse.text: We [[sincerely]] apologise for the delay to your order.
reverse.explanationRu: Искренние извинения — sincerely apologise. Frankly предупреждает о прямоте, а не выражает искренние чувства.

fixIt.text: [[Openly]] speaking, I think the new logo looks cheap and old-fashioned.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Откровенно говоря» — frankly (speaking), а не openly speaking. Openly — «открыто, не скрываясь».

wordFormation.text: I really appreciated the [[frankness]] of her feedback on my presentation.

reply.context: A colleague asks you: "Be honest. Should I apply for the manager's job?"
options: Frankly, I think you're ready. You already do half of that job anyway.
Frankly, I'd rather keep my honest opinion a secret from you.
Frankly, the applicant's suitability shall be evaluated in accordance with procedure.
reply.explanationRu: Frankly вводит честное мнение. Во втором ответе слово противоречит смыслу: человек как раз не хочет говорить честно. Третий звучит как казённый документ.

words.definitionEn: annoyed and impatient because you cannot do or achieve what you want
words.senseNote: Основное значение — досада, когда что-то не получается; именно его Oxford относит к C1. Важно не путать с disappointed и upset.
words.situation: You keep trying to do something, but problems or other people stop you, and you feel annoyed.

examples.text: After an hour on hold with the bank, I was so [[frustrated]] that I hung up.
Many nurses are [[frustrated]] that endless paperwork keeps them away from their patients.
The striker looked [[frustrated]] as yet another shot hit the post.

texts: Voters are [[frustrated]] with the slow pace of change.
I get [[frustrated]] when my laptop freezes during calls.
When you're learning a language, feeling [[frustrated]] is completely normal.

badCollocation.noteRu: Frustrated — досада от препятствий. О горе и печали говорят upset, sad или heartbroken.

collocationTask.prompt: She grew increasingly ___ with the lack of progress.
collocationTask.explanationRu: О чувствах человека — прилагательное на -ed: frustrated with something. Frustrating, disappointing и upsetting описывают то, что вызывает эти чувства.

nuance.text: I've been trying to fix this printer all morning, and I'm getting really [[frustrated]].
nuance.explanationRu: Frustrated — раздражение, когда что-то раз за разом не получается. Disappointed — разочарование, когда ожидания не оправдались; к борьбе с принтером оно не подходит.

reverse.text: I was [[disappointed]] with the film; the book was much better.
reverse.explanationRu: Фильм не оправдал ожиданий — disappointed. Frustrated означает досаду от препятствий, а не разочарование.

fixIt.text: I'm so [[frustrating]] with this website; it keeps logging me out!
fixIt.explanationRu: О своих чувствах — frustrated (-ed). Frustrating описывает то, что раздражает: this website is frustrating.

wordFormation.text: Tenants are increasingly [[frustrated]] by the landlord's failure to fix the heating.

reply.context: A colleague messages you: "How's the new accounting software going?"
options: Great! I'm so frustrated with how smoothly everything works.
Not great, to be honest. I'm frustrated because it crashes every time I save.
Current user status: frustrated. Awaiting technical intervention.
reply.explanationRu: Frustrated — досада, когда что-то мешает. Радоваться гладкой работе этим словом нельзя. Третий ответ звучит как сообщение робота, а не коллеги.

rewrite.original: The long delays really annoyed the passengers.
rewrite.frame: The passengers were really ____ the long delays.
rewrite.explanationRu: Frustrated by/with/at something — «раздосадован чем-то».

words.definitionEn: a member of a group or organisation who knows private information about how it works
words.situation: Describing someone who works within a company, party or industry and knows what really happens behind closed doors.

examples.text: Written by a former minister, the book offers an [[insider]]'s view of how parliament really works.
According to one [[insider]], the company will announce hundreds of job cuts next week.
After twenty years in the business, she's a true [[insider]] who knows exactly who makes the decisions.

texts: Industry [[insiders]] expect prices to rise again in the spring.
Party [[insiders]] say the leader has already chosen her successor.
Tourists queue at the famous cafés, but [[insiders]] know where the locals eat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Insider — это человек, а не сведения. «Инсайд» в смысле утечки по-английски — inside information или a tip-off.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ trading is illegal in most countries.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Insider trading — торговля акциями на основе закрытой информации. Inner, interior и inward с trading не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Only an [[insider]] could have known that the director had secretly resigned.
nuance.explanationRu: Insider знает секреты, потому что сам находится внутри группы. Expert — специалист со знаниями, но тайные решения компании ему неизвестны.

reverse.text: We asked an [[expert]] to check whether the painting was genuine.
reverse.explanationRu: Подлинность картины проверяет expert — специалист. Insider — свой человек в организации, а не знаток.

fixIt.text: The journalist's story was based on information from an [[insight]] at the ministry.
fixIt.explanationRu: Insight — понимание, озарение. Человек, который знает, что происходит внутри министерства, — insider.

wordFormation.text: Tickets sold out in minutes because a few [[insiders]] had been told about the sale in advance.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How do you always hear about changes before they're announced?"
options: I read the company newsletter very carefully, like an insider of the news.
My friend in HR is a bit of an insider, so I sometimes get a hint.
Information is disseminated to me via insider channels, as per protocol.
reply.explanationRu: Insider — человек внутри организации, который знает её секреты. «Insider of the news» — бессмыслица, а третий ответ звучит как казённый отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

words.definitionEn: to officially visit a place or organisation to check that it meets required standards
words.senseNote: Базовое «внимательно осматривать» (B2) не берём: здесь inspect — официальная проверка заведений и оборудования.
words.situation: Officials from a government agency visit a school, restaurant or factory to check that it follows the rules.

examples.text: Health officials [[inspect]] every restaurant in the city at least once a year.
The factory was closed after officials [[inspected]] it and found serious safety problems.
Our school will be [[inspected]] next month, so all the teachers are polishing their lesson plans.

texts: Officials arrived without warning to [[inspect]] the kitchen.
The agency sends experts to [[inspect]] nuclear power stations every year.
Council staff must [[inspect]] the building before anyone can move in.

badCollocation.noteRu: Домашнее задание проверяют — check или mark. Inspect — официальная проверка заведений, зданий и оборудования.

collocationTask.prompt: The restaurant is ___ by health officials twice a year.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальную проверку описывает inspected. Controlled — «находится под управлением», revised — «исправлен», watched — просто «за ним наблюдали».

nuance.text: Two safety officials came to [[inspect]] the lift after it kept stopping between floors.
nuance.explanationRu: Inspect — проверить состояние по правилам. Control — управлять, держать под контролем: «проконтролировать лифт» по-английски не control the lift.

reverse.text: In the strong wind, the pilot struggled to [[control]] the small plane.
reverse.explanationRu: Управлять самолётом — control. Inspect значит «официально проверять», к управлению это не относится.

fixIt.text: The agency [[controls]] every care home once a year and publishes a report on each one.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Контролировать» в смысле официальной проверки — inspect. Control значит «управлять, держать под контролем».

wordFormation.text: Two [[inspectors]] arrived at the factory without any warning.

rewrite.original: Officials check the kitchen every six months.
rewrite.frame: The kitchen ____ every six months.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the kitchen is inspected — «кухню проверяют».

words.definitionEn: an official check of a building, vehicle or organisation to make sure it meets standards
words.senseNote: Не просто «внимательный осмотр» (B1), а официальная проверка: школы, кафе, машины, безопасности.
words.situation: Talking about the official checks that restaurants, schools and vehicles must pass to prove they are safe.

examples.text: The restaurant was closed after it failed a hygiene [[inspection]] last month.
Every car older than three years must pass an annual safety [[inspection]].
Before the sale goes ahead, a surveyor will carry out a full [[inspection]] of the house.

texts: The school is preparing for a government [[inspection]] next week.
Customs officers carried out a random [[inspection]] of the lorry.
The bridge was closed for a safety [[inspection]] after the storm.

badCollocation.noteRu: Проверка знаний — test или assessment. Inspection — официальная проверка зданий, заведений и техники.

collocationTask.prompt: The building failed its fire safety ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальную проверку, которую можно пройти или провалить, называют inspection. Control — управление, revision — правка текста, overview — краткий обзор.

nuance.text: After a surprise [[inspection]], the care home was ordered to hire more nurses.
nuance.explanationRu: Внезапная проверка заведения — inspection (о финансах — audit). Revision — правка текста или повторение перед экзаменом, а не «ревизия».

reverse.text: The contract needs a small [[revision]] before we can sign it.
reverse.explanationRu: Правка в договоре — revision. Inspection — проверка зданий и заведений, текст так не исправляют.

fixIt.text: The café had to close for a week after a health [[control]] found mice in the kitchen.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Санитарный контроль» по-английски — health inspection. Control — управление, власть над чем-то, а не проверка.

wordFormation.text: The fire service will carry out an [[inspection]] of the theatre before it reopens.

reply.context: A friend who runs a café messages you: "The health inspectors are coming tomorrow and I'm panicking!"
options: Relax, your kitchen is spotless. You'll pass the inspection easily.
Lucky you! An inspection means they'll probably order lunch and leave a big tip.
Kindly ensure that all premises are rendered compliant prior to the inspection.
reply.explanationRu: Inspection — официальная проверка, её можно pass или fail. Второй ответ путает её с визитом гостей, третий звучит как распоряжение начальства, а не поддержка друга.

words.definitionEn: a natural feeling that tells you what to do or believe without conscious thought
words.senseNote: Не биологический инстинкт животных (B2), а человеческое чутьё: trust your instincts, my first instinct was to run.
words.situation: Explaining that you acted on a feeling rather than careful reasoning, for example when you sense that someone is lying.

examples.text: When the fire alarm went off, my first [[instinct]] was to grab my laptop.
Experienced nurses often trust their [[instincts]] when a patient seems fine but something feels wrong.
The figures looked convincing, but my [[instinct]] told me the deal was too good to be true.

texts: Trust your [[instincts]]: if the flat feels wrong, don't rent it.
The coach ignored his [[instincts]] and kept the tired player on the pitch.
Her political [[instincts]] told her the vote would be closer than expected.

badCollocation.text: have an [[instinct]] that he is lying
badCollocation.noteRu: С придаточным говорят I have a feeling that или my instinct tells me that. Сочетание have an instinct that звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.prompt: If the deal feels wrong, ___ your instincts and walk away.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчиво: trust (или follow) your instincts — «доверься чутью». Rely требует on, а hear и credit с instincts не сочетаются.

nuance.text: My [[instinct]] told me not to sign the contract until a lawyer had read it.
nuance.explanationRu: Instinct — внутреннее чутьё, которое подсказывает решение. Reflex — автоматическая реакция тела (моргнуть, отдёрнуть руку), она ничего не «подсказывает».

reverse.text: The doctor tapped my knee with a small hammer to test my [[reflexes]].
reverse.explanationRu: Врач проверяет reflexes — автоматические реакции тела. Instincts — чутьё и природные побуждения, молоточком их не проверишь.

fixIt.text: Something about the offer felt wrong, and my [[flair]] told me to walk away.
fixIt.explanationRu: Flair — талант или стиль (a flair for languages). Чутьё, которое «подсказывает», — instinct: my instinct told me.

wordFormation.text: When the lights went out, she [[instinctively]] reached for her phone.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Should I take the job? The salary is great, but the boss made me feel uneasy."
options: Take it! Your instinct of the salary is the most important thing.
Pursuant to my instinct, the offer ought to be declined forthwith.
I'd listen to that feeling. If your instinct says something's off, it probably is.
reply.explanationRu: Instinct — внутреннее чутьё, и третий ответ использует его естественно. «Instinct of the salary» — бессмыслица, а второй вариант звучит как юридический документ.

words.definitionEn: done or felt naturally and automatically, without thinking or being taught
words.situation: Describing a reaction or feeling that comes automatically, before you have any time to think about it.

examples.text: Covering your face when something flies towards you is a purely [[instinctive]] reaction.
Great comedians seem to have an [[instinctive]] sense of timing that can't be taught.
My [[instinctive]] response was to say yes, but I asked for a day to think it over.

texts: Most parents feel an [[instinctive]] urge to protect their children.
His [[instinctive]] dislike of the new manager proved to be justified.
Blinking is [[instinctive]]; nobody has to teach a baby to do it.

badCollocation.noteRu: Интерфейс, понятный без инструкций, — intuitive. Instinctive — о реакциях и чувствах, которые возникают сами собой.

collocationTask.prompt: I took an instinctive ___ to him the moment we met.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчиво: take a dislike to someone — «невзлюбить». С disgust, hostility и anger глагол take так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Shutting your eyes when sand blows into your face is [[instinctive]].
nuance.explanationRu: Instinctive — реакция, заложенная природой (зажмуриться, отдёрнуть руку). Impulsive — о человеке или решении: действует сгоряча, не думая о последствиях.

reverse.text: She's so [[impulsive]] that she once booked a holiday during her lunch break.
reverse.explanationRu: Человек, который поступает сгоряча, — impulsive. Instinctive описывает реакции, а не характер.

fixIt.text: When a ball flew towards her face, she raised her hands in an [[intuitive]] movement.
fixIt.explanationRu: Intuitive — о понимании без рассуждений или об удобном интерфейсе. Непроизвольное движение тела — instinctive.

wordFormation.text: Babies have an [[instinctive]] fear of loud, sudden noises.

reply.context: In a job interview, you're asked: "How do you make decisions under pressure?"
options: I make instinctive decisions only after weeks of careful analysis.
I rely on data, but in a real crisis my instinctive reaction is to stay calm and prioritise.
Honestly? I just go with my instinctive vibes, lol.
reply.explanationRu: Instinctive — «без раздумий», поэтому instinctive decisions после недель анализа — противоречие. Третий ответ слишком разговорный для собеседования.

words.definitionEn: relating to large organisations such as banks, universities or governments and the way they work
words.situation: Talking about banks, universities, courts or government bodies as organisations, rather than about the people who work in them.

examples.text: Pension funds and other [[institutional]] investors own most of the company's shares.
When experienced staff retire, a lot of [[institutional]] knowledge leaves with them.
The report calls for deep [[institutional]] reform, not just the dismissal of a few senior managers.

texts: Small charities often struggle to attract [[institutional]] funding.
Her thesis looks at [[institutional]] change in European universities.
Without [[institutional]] support, the volunteers' project quickly ran out of money.

badCollocation.noteRu: Студент вуза — a university или college student. Institutional описывает крупные организации и их устройство, а не учёбу в институте.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ investors such as pension funds and insurance companies
collocationTask.explanationRu: Пенсионные фонды и страховые компании — institutional investors. Official, organisational и structural с investors так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After years in [[institutional]] care, he found it hard to cook and shop for himself.
nuance.explanationRu: Institutional care — жизнь в интернате, доме престарелых или детском доме. Organisational относится к организации работы (organisational skills), с care так не говорят.

reverse.text: The job requires excellent [[organisational]] skills and attention to detail.
reverse.explanationRu: Умение планировать и всё успевать — organisational skills. Institutional skills так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The charity gets most of its money from [[organisational]] donors such as banks and foundations.
fixIt.explanationRu: Банки и фонды как жертвователи или инвесторы — institutional donors, institutional investors. Organisational так не употребляют.

wordFormation.text: Museums increasingly depend on [[institutional]] sponsors rather than on ticket sales.

rewrite.original: Large organisations such as pension funds hold most of the shares.
rewrite.frame: Most of the shares are held by ____ such as pension funds.
rewrite.explanationRu: Банки и фонды в роли инвесторов — institutional investors.

words.definitionEn: to formally tell someone to do something, often as an official order
words.senseNote: Базовое «обучать» (instruct someone in something) не берём: здесь — официально велеть, дать указание.
words.situation: A manager, judge or official formally tells people what they must do, often in writing.

examples.text: The judge [[instructed]] the jury to ignore the witness's last remark.
Staff have been [[instructed]] not to discuss the merger with journalists.
Passengers are [[instructed]] to remain in their seats until the plane has come to a complete stop.

texts: The bank [[instructed]] its lawyers to recover the money.
Doctors [[instructed]] her to rest for at least two weeks.
Police [[instructed]] residents to keep their windows closed because of the smoke.

badCollocation.noteRu: Instruct — переходный глагол: instruct the staff to do something, без предлога to перед людьми.

collocationTask.prompt: Unless ___ otherwise, please keep this door locked.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Unless instructed otherwise — «если не будет других указаний». Teach и learn — про обучение, а explained otherwise в таком обороте не говорят.

nuance.text: The manager [[instructed]] everyone to delete the old files by Friday.
nuance.explanationRu: Instruct someone to do something — дать указание, велеть. Teach someone to do something — научить. Начальник здесь отдаёт распоряжение, а не учит удалять файлы.

reverse.text: My grandmother [[taught]] me to knit when I was six.
reverse.explanationRu: Научить вязать — teach. Instructed me to knit значило бы, что бабушка велела вязать.

fixIt.text: My manager [[entrusted]] me to prepare the budget report by Monday.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Поручить сделать» — instruct someone to do something. После entrust нужна другая конструкция: entrust someone with a task.

wordFormation.text: The staff followed the manager's [[instructions]] and left the building at once.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "Why is everyone working from home tomorrow?"
options: It has been instructed by the relevant authority that personnel remain domiciled.
Management instructed us to stay home while they fix the heating.
Management instructed us in staying home. It's part of a new training course.
reply.explanationRu: Instruct someone to do something — «велеть сделать», как во втором ответе. Первый звучит как казённый приказ, а в третьем instruct путают с «обучать».

rewrite.original: The manager told us to lock the office every evening.
rewrite.frame: We ____ to lock the office every evening.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив: we were instructed to do something — «нам велели».

words.definitionEn: playing an important part in making something happen or succeed
words.senseNote: Не музыкальное «инструментальный»: здесь be instrumental in doing something — сыграть ключевую роль.
words.situation: Giving someone credit for playing a key part in getting something done or making a change happen.

examples.text: Thanks to her fundraising, she was [[instrumental]] in setting up the town's first food bank.
Social media was [[instrumental]] in spreading warnings about the flood within minutes.
The new coach was [[instrumental]] in the team's return to the top division.

texts: Her advice was [[instrumental]] in my decision to change careers.
Volunteers were [[instrumental]] in rebuilding the village school.
This discovery was [[instrumental]] in developing the new vaccine.

badCollocation.noteRu: После instrumental нужен предлог in и форма на -ing: instrumental in winning the match, а не to win.

collocationTask.prompt: Her early research was ___ in bringing about the change.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be instrumental in doing something — «сыграть ключевую роль». Instructive — поучительный, insistent — настойчивый, incidental — второстепенный.

nuance.text: His contacts in the industry were [[instrumental]] in finding investors for the project.
nuance.explanationRu: Instrumental in — сыгравший ключевую роль в результате. Instructive — поучительный, дающий знания: an instructive visit, an instructive example.

reverse.text: The factory visit was very [[instructive]] for the engineering students.
reverse.explanationRu: Поездка, из которой студенты многое узнали, — instructive. Instrumental требует результата: instrumental in doing something.

fixIt.text: Her contacts were [[instructive]] in finding sponsors for the festival.
fixIt.explanationRu: Instructive — «поучительный». Сыграть ключевую роль в результате — be instrumental in doing something.

wordFormation.text: Local volunteers were [[instrumental]] in cleaning up the beach after the storm.

reply.context: At a leaving party, your boss asks you to say a few words about Anna, who is retiring.
options: Anna was very instrumental: she played the piano at every office party.
Anna's instrumentality in team formation is hereby formally acknowledged.
Anna was instrumental in building this team; most of us are here because she hired us.
reply.explanationRu: Be instrumental in — сыграть ключевую роль, как в третьем ответе. Instrumental не значит «играющий на инструменте», а второй вариант — канцелярит на тёплом прощании.

words.definitionEn: not enough in amount or quality for a particular purpose
words.senseNote: Формальное слово для официальных текстов; в разговоре обычно говорят not enough.
words.situation: Explaining formally that the money, time, evidence or information available is less than what is needed.

examples.text: The case was dropped because there was [[insufficient]] evidence to prove he was guilty.
The payment failed because there were [[insufficient]] funds in the account.
Staff complained that two weeks was [[insufficient]] time to learn the new software.

texts: The hospital's staffing levels are [[insufficient]] for the busy winter months.
A single heater is [[insufficient]] for a room this size.
Her written explanation was [[insufficient]], so the committee asked for more details.

badCollocation.noteRu: В разговоре говорят not enough money. Insufficient — официальное слово: insufficient funds в сообщении банка, insufficient evidence в суде.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Стандартная фраза банка — insufficient funds, «недостаточно средств». Lacking, absent и short перед funds так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Your card was declined due to [[insufficient]] funds.
nuance.explanationRu: Insufficient — «не хватает по количеству», а insufficient funds — стандартная банковская фраза. Inadequate чаще о качестве или о человеке: feel inadequate — чувствовать себя хуже других.

reverse.text: Surrounded by brilliant colleagues, he often felt completely [[inadequate]].
reverse.explanationRu: О чувстве собственной несостоятельности говорят feel inadequate. Insufficient описывает количество, а не человека.

fixIt.text: There was [[deficient]] time to finish the experiment, so the results are incomplete.
fixIt.explanationRu: Deficient — «с изъяном, неполноценный» (vitamin-deficient). «Недостаточно времени» — insufficient time.

wordFormation.text: Many new drivers are [[insufficiently]] prepared for driving at night.

reply.context: A client emails: "Why was my online payment rejected?"
options: The payment was rejected because the amount was insufficient: you paid too much.
Dude, your card's got insufficient cash, lol.
Sorry for the trouble. The bank reports there were insufficient funds on the card at the time.
reply.explanationRu: Insufficient funds — «недостаточно средств», вежливо и по делу. В первом ответе insufficient сочетается с «переплатой», а второй слишком фамильярен для клиента.

rewrite.original: There wasn't enough evidence to take the case to court.
rewrite.frame: The evidence was ____ to take the case to court.
rewrite.explanationRu: Not enough → insufficient: формальный вариант.

words.definitionEn: a rude remark or action that shows a lack of respect for someone
words.senseNote: Не только грубое слово: предложение или поступок, унижающие человека, — тоже an insult (an insult to our intelligence).
words.situation: Reacting to a remark, offer or decision that makes you feel disrespected or treated as stupid.

examples.text: After twenty years of loyal service, a pay rise of one percent felt like an [[insult]].
The plot is so predictable that it's an [[insult]] to the audience's intelligence.
After the crash, the two angry drivers started shouting [[insults]] at each other.

texts: Don't take it as an [[insult]]; he criticises everyone's work.
Offering such a low price for her painting was an [[insult]].
To add [[insult]] to injury, the airline lost our luggage too.

badCollocation.noteRu: По-английски говорят cause offence или просто insult someone. Сочетания cause an insult нет.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение an insult to someone's intelligence — «нас держат за дураков». С mind, brain и wisdom так не говорят.

nuance.text: I only said his cooking was 'interesting', but he took it as an [[insult]].
nuance.explanationRu: Insult — само обидное слово или поступок: take something as an insult. Offence — обида: take offence (без артикля и as), а take something as an offence не говорят.

reverse.text: I hope you won't take [[offence]], but your report needs a lot more work.
reverse.explanationRu: Устойчиво: take offence — обидеться. Take insult по-английски не говорят.

fixIt.text: Calling her a beginner in front of the whole team was a deliberate [[abuse]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Abuse — неисчисляемое (verbal abuse), с артиклем a не употребляется. Одно обидное замечание — an insult.

wordFormation.text: Many readers found the article's tone deeply [[insulting]].

reply.context: A friend texts: "They offered me fifty pounds to design their whole website!"
options: That's not an offer, that's an insult. Say no.
Wow, what an insult! You should accept it immediately.
Such remuneration constitutes a grave insult to your professional standing, madam.
reply.explanationRu: Insult — унизительное предложение, и первый ответ это передаёт. Во втором insult противоречит совету согласиться, третий звучит как официальное письмо, а не ответ другу.

rewrite.original: His comment offended me, although he didn't mean it that way.
rewrite.frame: I took his comment as ____, although he didn't mean it that way.
rewrite.explanationRu: Take something as an insult — «воспринять как оскорбление».
